note: Color, the photo-sharing app (Palo Alto). BCV (Michael Krupka) invested in its $41M first round of 2011 alongside Sequoia and Silicon Valley Bank; Apple bought the company in 2012 (the firm lists 'Color Labs Inc. (Apple)', Acquired; the press called it an acquisition, so it reads acquired under the acqui-hire rule's last sentence).

Embedded tax filing (New York). 'BCV has led a $5.1M seed financing for Column Tax' (the firm's post, 2021-11-23); the $21.7M Series A followed in May 2022 (Forbes). Acquired by Aiwyn in 2025 (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/aiwyn-seeks-100-firms-for-groundbreaking-tax-pilot-following-column-tax-acquisition-302642515.html).
Concurrent, Inc. (San Francisco), the company behind the Cascading data framework; BCV entered with Salil Deshpande in 2014 (Form D). No trace of the company after the mid-2010s; state unknown.
Cyber insurance (Boston). Acquired by Travelers in 2024 (the firm lists 'Corvus (Travelers)', Acquired). BCV's listing: 2016, Seed. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Retail predictive analytics (Cambridge, MA). Acquired by Demandware in October 2014 (https://www.bizjournals.com/boston/inno/stories/news/2014/10/14/demandware-acquires-cambridges-cquotient-in-e.html). The filings give BCV's 2010 seed ($3M) and no later round before the sale.

AI cloud and data centres (founded in Denver; San Francisco HQ). BCV's listing: 2019, Seed (the $4.5M seed of May 2019); the partner-anchored Form D (2019-11, Stefan Cohen) is the $70M Series A of December 2019, which graduates the seed, so the band's Series A is overruled. Mark: the $3.9B round of September 2026 at $30.9B (trendingtopics.eu); the $1.375B Series E of October 2025 was at $10B+.

Semantic layer for data (Cube Dev, San Francisco; Wikidata's DE is another Cube). BCV's listing: 2020 (Aaref Hilaly), 'Early'; the 2020 round is the $6.2M seed TechCrunch reported in September 2020, which BCV led; the $15.5M Series A (July 2021) and a $25M round (2024) followed.
AI customer-support agents (San Francisco). BCV entered in 2024 (Aaref Hilaly; the firm's post 'Why We Backed Decagon AI'). Mark: the $250M Series D of January 2026 at $4.5B.

Loan origination software (Dallas). 'defi SOLUTIONS picks $55m Series C led by Bain Capital' (FinTech Global, 2018-01-22; the firm lists it with Matt Harris, Growth). Merged with Sagent Auto in 2019 under the defi SOLUTIONS name; operating.

Graph database (Dgraph Labs). BCV (Salil Deshpande) entered with the 2017 seed the filings give; Redpoint led an $11.5M Series A in 2018 (TechTarget, 2019, on the company's funding), which graduates it though no BCV-anchored Form D records it. Istari Digital acquired Dgraph in October 2025 (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/istari-digital-acquires-dgraph-to-strengthen-data-foundation-for-ai-and-engineering-302593246.html).

Crypto holding company (Stamford, CT; Grayscale's parent). BCV's listing: 2014, Seed (Matt Harris; the 2015 formation round that also brought in Mastercard and others). The prefilled $10B is the November 2021 sale of about $700M of shares led by SoftBank (https://www.cnbc.com/2021/11/01/digital-currency-group-sees-10-billion-valuation-as-softbank-google-invest.html); after Genesis's 2023 collapse no newer priced event is known, so it stands, stale. Graduation left for the graduation pass.
Container tooling (Palo Alto). BCV led the $105M Series C at $2.1B (the firm's post, 2022-03-31); no later priced round; stale.

E-signature (San Francisco). 'Bain Capital Ventures, along with Bain Capital Public Equity, was fortunate to lead DocuSign's last two rounds of funding' (the firm's post, 2018-04-27): growth rounds of 2014-2015, as the filings give.
Battery-powered interactive payment cards (Cheswick, PA); product and partnership news through 2018 (SoftBank collaboration). No sale or shutdown found; read as operating.

Application performance monitoring. BCV's position was in dynaTrace software (Waltham), which Compuware bought in July 2011 (the firm's archived page); today's NYSE-listed Dynatrace is the business spun out of Compuware in 2019, so the float belongs to a successor and the row reads acquired (COLLECTION.md s8 duty 4). BCV's 2010 round (the filings' $4M in a company incorporated in 2006, band withheld) is not named.
Consumer loan-payment platform (San Francisco); a $31M Series C closed in March 2022. BCV's listing: 2019, 'Early'; the round is not named.

LED lighting (EcoSense Lighting); combined into Korrus in 2021. BCV entered in 2011 (Jeffrey Glass, John Connolly on the Form D) in a company incorporated in 2008; the band is withheld and the round is not named.

basis: EDGAR Online was listed on NASDAQ (EDGR) from 1999; BCV's 2010 investment was a private placement into the listed company (its 8-K of 2010-01-29 files the investor rights agreement signed by Bain Capital Venture Integral Investors). A placement into a public company is not a venture round in a private company (COLLECTION.md s1 T3; decisions.md D4).

The Princeton Review was listed on NASDAQ (REVU) from its 2001 IPO (the firm's own archive: 'IPO on 6/19/01'); BCV's 2007 investment was preferred stock issued by the listed company (its 8-K of 2007-07-26 defines the 'Bain Fund'), later renamed Education Holdings 1. A placement into a public company is not a venture round (COLLECTION.md s1 T3; decisions.md D4).

note: The original Emburse, a corporate card startup (San Francisco), bought in 2019 by the Certify / Chrome River group, which took its name. BCV's listing: 2016, Seed (Matt Harris). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Healthcare provider data (Aliso Viejo, CA). Acquired by LexisNexis (the firm's archived listing). The filings' 2009 round sits in a company incorporated in 2005, so the band is withheld; no source names BCV's round.

Claims-contents software for insurers (Natick, MA). The firm listed it from 2006 (Midstage) and later as Exited; acquired by Solera. BCV's first round (2006) precedes the 2009 Form D and is not named.
Donor CRM for education (Boston); the firm lists it as Acquired. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Cloud security compliance (Dublin, CA). Palo Alto Networks bought it in March 2018 (https://www.csoonline.com/article/564888/palo-alto-networks-buys-evidentio-extends-its-cloud-security-solution.html). BCV's listing gives 2014; the first partner-anchored Form D (2016) is a later round in a company incorporated in 2013; the entry round is not named.
Brand-to-expert product marketing (ExpertVoice, formerly Experticity; Salt Lake City). Operating.
Collaborative web mapping (Oakland). 'Felt is announcing its $4.5M seed round led by BCV' (the firm's post, 2021-08-10); the $15M Series A followed in May 2022 (TechCrunch).
AI commerce storefronts (FERMAT, San Francisco); $17M Series A in March 2024, the round the filings give.
Payments infrastructure for software platforms (San Francisco). 'We are thrilled to announce that we're leading a $17.5 million Series A in Finix' (the firm's post, 2019-07-16).

Debt-capital management software (San Francisco). 'Finley announces $3 million seed fundraise led by Bain Capital Ventures' (PR Newswire, 2021-06-14); the $17M Series A followed (TechCrunch, January 2023). Concord acquired Finley in March 2026 (https://www.fintechfutures.com/m-a/concord-acquires-finley-technologies-to-enhance-credit-administration-capabilities).
Cross-border e-commerce (Hoboken, NJ). Acquired by Global-e in 2021 (the firm's listing).

Flux.ai, browser-based electronics design (San Francisco). BCV's 'Seed Investment In Flux' (the firm's post, 2021-10-13; the $12M round TechCrunch reported); a Series B followed in 2026 (FinSMEs, and $37M per Fortune). The prefilled public CZ float belongs to an unrelated listed 'Flux'.
Education and B2B payments (Boston), IPO May 2021 (NASDAQ: FLYW); entry from the filings (Matt Harris, 2015).
Network access control (San Jose). BCV's 2015 growth round (Enrique Salem on the Form D); IPO 2017; taken private by Advent in 2020.
Open-source license and security management (FOSSA; the firm lists Chicago). BCV's listing: 2016, Seed; the $8.5M Series A followed in 2019 (TechCrunch) and a $23M Series B in 2020.

Supply-chain visibility (Chicago). 'FourKites has grown more than twentyfold since we led the Series A just over two years ago' (the firm's post, 2019-02-05); BCV's listing gives 2016. The band's Growth reads the later 2019 filing.
Cloud desktop delivery (Frame, formerly Mainframe2; San Mateo). 'Frame Secures $16M in New Funding from Bain Capital Ventures, Microsoft Ventures and In-Q-Tel' (2017); acquired by Nutanix in 2018.

Customer success software (founded 2009 as JBara). BCV's listing tags the 2013 entry Growth, the $9M Series B of November 2013; the Form D band read it as Series A for a company that had raised since 2011. Vista acquired Gainsight in 2020 ($1.1B).
Warehouse inventory drones (Pittsburgh). 'We led Gather AI's $17 million Series A-1' (the firm's post, 2024-03-27); the $40M Series B (February 2026) is the later filing the band read.

Bank-payment collection (London). BCV led the $95M Series F of December 2020 (Finextra; the firm's post 2021-01-05). Mollie agreed to buy GoCardless in December 2025 and closed the purchase in September 2026 (https://www.democrata.es/en/economy/mollie-closes-the-purchase-of-gocardless-and-forms-a-group-with-more-than-350-000-client-companies/).
ETF sponsor (New York), an operating asset manager rather than a fund. BCV's listing: 2014, Seed (Matt Harris). Graduation left for the graduation pass.
Anti-ransomware platform (Austin). BCV led the $40M Series B (the firm's post, 2023-12-19). Mark: the $100M Series C of November 2024 at $1B (Austin Business Journal).

Clinical communication (Cincinnati): Doc Halo, renamed Halo Communications and then Halo Health, acquired by symplr in 2022 (the firm lists 'Halo Health (Symplr)'). The doc-halo and halo-communications rows are the same company (one Form D CIK, 1704200) and merge into this row at the rebuild; the entry round comes with them.

School-based telehealth (San Francisco); $33M Series C (2020) and $51.5M Series C1 (2022). BCV's listing gives 2017, three years before the first partner-anchored filing the band read as Growth; the 2017 round is not named.
